title: Avianca 011

agencies.name: Civil Aviation Accident and Incident Investigation Commission

summary: Avianca Flight 011 crashed on a hill approximately 7.5 miles southeast of Madrid Barajas Airport during an ILS approach on November 27, 1983. The captain, a highly experienced pilot, incorrectly determined the aircraft's position during the instrument approach in night conditions with low visibility. The aircraft struck terrain on three different hills, killing 181 passengers and crew on board.
probable_cause: Pilot error in the form of an incorrect determination of the aircraft's position relative to the runway during the instrument landing system approach in night conditions and low visibility, resulting in controlled flight into terrain.

factors.evidence: The 747 crashed on a hill approximately 7.5 miles southeast of the airport; the plane hit three different hills on its way down during the crash.
The captain having incorrectly determined the position of the plane was judged to be pilot error.
The captain's position determination was incorrect, indicating loss of situational awareness during the instrument approach.
It was night at the time of the accident with visibility of 5 miles.

events.text: Aircraft took off from Charles de Gaulle Airport in Paris on November 26 at 22:25 local time.
First contact with Spanish air traffic controllers; aircraft obtained meteorological information on weather conditions at Barajas with visibility of 5 miles.
Aircraft contacted Barajas and was cleared to land on runway 33; this was the air traffic controller's last contact with the aircraft.
Aircraft struck terrain on three different hills with final impact on third hill, aircraft destroyed by impact and ensuing fire.

notes: Investigation determined pilot error in position determination but specific mechanism could not be identified
